div.head: Ine 35
div.ab: LXXVIIII. Se ðe þeof slihð, he mot aþe gecyðan, þæt he hine fleonde for ðeof sloge, ⁊ ðæs deadan magas him swerian unceastes áð. Gif he hit ðonne dyrne, ⁊ sy eft yppe, ðonne forgilde he hine.
LXXVIIII. Se ðe ðeof slihð, he mot aðe gecyðan, þæt he hine fleondne for ðeof sloge, ⁊ þæs deadan mægas him swerian unceases áð. Gif he hit þonne dierne, ⁊ sie eft yppe, þonne forgielde he hine.

Qui furem occiderit, licet ei probare cum iuramento (iureiurando), quod eum fugientem pro fure occidit, et parentibus ipsius occisi iuret unceases aþ (id est sacramentum sine electione [uel nominatione]). Si concelauerit, et sit deinceps manifestum, tunc persoluat eum.
{LXXVIIII} Se ðe ðeof slihð, he mot aðe gecyðan, þæt he hine fleonde for ðeof sloge, ⁊ þæs deadan mægas him swerian unceases áð. Gif he hit þonne dierne, ⁊ sie eft yppe, þonne forgielde he hine.

He who kills a thief may declare on oath that he slew him for a thief as he was running away, and the kin of the dead man must swear him an oath not to engage in hostilities against him. If he, however, conceals [the slaying] and it afterwards becomes known, then he must make restitution for him.

He who kills a thief shall be allowed to declare with an oath that he whom he killed was a thief trying to escape, and the kinsmen of the dead man shall swear an oath to carry on no vendetta against him. If, however, he keeps it [the homicide] secret, and it afterwards comes to light, then he shall pay for him.

He who slays a thief may declare with an oath that he slew him fleeing as a thief, and the kinsmen of the dead man are to swear to him an oath not to carry on a feud. If, however, he conceals it and it is revealed later, he is then to pay for him.

Wer einen Dieb erschlägt, der darf durch Eid beweisen, dass er ihn, den fliehenden, als Dieb erschlug; und die Verwandten des Erschlagenen sollen ihm Urfehde-Eid schwören. Wenn er es aber verbirgt, und [es] wird späterhin offenbar, dann vergelte er ihn.

Whoever slays a thief may prove by oath that he slew him, as he was fleeing, as a thief; and the kinsmen of the slain man are to swear him an oath renouncing feud. But if he conceals it, and [it] becomes known later, then let him pay for him.
